questions_before_wrapping_content: Does this section need containment at all?
Does this content need a box?
Does this layout become stronger if the box is removed?
Is this line replacing a missing composition decision?

legitimate_containment_reasons: content is an interactive target (clickable, draggable, selectable, expandable)
content is a functional unit that can be removed/reordered/swapped
content is media whose bounds would otherwise leak into adjacent content
content is genuinely a peer of siblings (product tile, article card)
content changes state visibly (panel expands, card flips, tile highlights)
not_legitimate_reasons: the box makes the section feel finished
the box matches the other sections
the border makes it feel designed

default_rendering_unit.name: region
default_rendering_unit.definition: vertical space with deliberate top/bottom spacing, content on a chosen alignment axis, typography carrying hierarchy, no frame unless the four questions justified one

asymmetry_prompts: primary + smaller supports rather than three equal cards
editorial paragraphs offset to one column
hero 60/40 or 40/60 rather than centered stacked
heading against a large calm area rather than framed by decoration

rhythm_alternation.rule: long pages must alternate between dense and quiet zones; repetition of one zone type reads as monotone

elimination_pass_steps: list every decorative element on the page
note whether real communication is lost
if lost, understand what was lost, then decide whether a stronger structural device should carry that job
final_test: Grayscale the design. Remove borders, dividers, glows, gradients, shadows. Does hierarchy still read? Does the reading path still lead the eye? Does the composition still have identity? If no, composition was hiding behind decoration.
